title: docs(skills): the automation skill's CEL table is the bare-callable public subset
body:
Fixes #15520

`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` repeated the completeness claim the formula skill has just had corrected, one skill over: conditions are bare CEL and "only the stdlib is callable", pointing at the formula skill for "the full table". Both halves under-promise. The CEL environment also resolves receiver methods called on a value, so the catalogue is the **bare-callable public subset** — the membership rule `packages/formula/src/validate.ts` carries as load-bearing — and not everything that resolves. Wrong in the **safe** direction, so no author was broken by it; corrected anyway.

The correction is one clause, in this skill's voice and much shorter than the formula skill's passage, because that skill now carries the full statement and this file keeps pointing at it. Receiver method names and the four withheld bare primitives are deliberately **not** enumerated here — the table's owner states them once.

⛔ No edit to `skills/objectstack-formula/**`, to `packages/**`, or to any other skill. `references/_index.md` is generator-owned and was not hand-edited.

## Before and after

| site | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| L351, the item's bold lead | 4. **Conditions are bare CEL — only the stdlib is callable.** | 4. **Conditions are bare CEL — the stdlib is what you may call bare.** |
| L354, the pointer closing the same item | …plus CEL built-ins (`has`, `size`, `int`, `string`, …) — see **objectstack-formula** for the full table. | …plus CEL built-ins (`has`, `size`, `int`, `string`, …) — see **objectstack-formula** for that table: it is `CEL_STDLIB_FUNCTIONS`, the bare-callable public subset, so receiver methods (called on a value, never bare) are not in it. |

The rest of the item is unchanged and stays true: an unknown function name and a brace-wrapped field ref both fail the build.

## Every occurrence — the whole skill scanned, the near misses named

Scanned `skills/objectstack-automation/` entire (SKILL.md, `references/`, `evals/`) for the claim family: `only the stdlib`, `only … callable`, `are callable`, `full table`, `canonical list`, `exhaustive`, `documents them all`, `complete list`, `full list`, `all the functions/built-ins`, `stdlib`.

| site | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| SKILL.md L351 and L354 | the two false claims — both corrected above, and they are all of them |
| SKILL.md L35, the intro callout | points at objectstack-formula "for the CEL contract, stdlib and legacy → CEL table" — a pointer carrying no completeness word; left as it is |
| SKILL.md L291 | `{round(x)}`/`{abs(x)}` "mirror the CEL stdlib 1:1" — a claim about the single-brace VALUE-interpolation dialect, a different surface with its own named supported set; not a member of this family |
| SKILL.md L645, L945, and `evals/approvals/test-revise-loop.md` | "the full loop", "the full list of Zod schemas", "the full ADR-0044 shape" — unrelated uses of the word |
| `references/_index.md` | generator-owned; carries no such claim, so nothing needed a hand-edit and none was made |

The 3 measured nothing and was not a finding.

## Landing

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` exits **3**:

- `⛔  GOVERNED — a human merge is the review record for this PR.`
- `skills/** ×1 — the published skills catalog`

So this **stays a draft**: not flipped ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge armed, and no approving review from the authoring seat.

`skip-changeset` applies by the rule rather than by the example list — this PR publishes nothing from any package; no workspace `package.json` ships `skills/`, so the catalogue is not a package artifact.

## Review notes

Two things a wording change like this can get wrong, both cheap to check: that the sentence agrees with the formula skill's corrected passage where it matters — bare-callability as the membership rule, receiver methods called on a value and therefore absent from that table — and that this file does not quietly become a second place where the withheld primitives are listed. It names none of them, by design; one published statement of them, in the skill that owns the table.
